description: Voice-agent KPIs judged the way a caller experiences them: how fast the agent answers, how often it answers, and only then how the workers are holding up.

panels.title: Experience — what the caller actually feels

panels.description: THE voice-agent number. Median time from the caller finishing their turn (VAD endpoint) to the first PCM of the agent's reply being queued. Under ~600 ms feels instant; over ~1.2 s feels like a bad phone line.

targets.rawSql: SELECT quantile(0.50)(time_to_first_audio_ms) AS value FROM pipeline.pipeline_events WHERE event_type='tts.first_audio_queued' AND status='ok' AND time_to_first_audio_ms > 0 AND event_time_ms BETWEEN $__from AND $__to AND model IN (${model:sqlstring}) AND engine IN (${engine:sqlstring}) AND device IN (${device:sqlstring})

panels.title: Turn response latency p50

panels.description: Tail of the response latency. The p95 is what your least-lucky callers live through; keep it under ~1.5 s or the agent feels unreliable even when the median looks fine.

targets.rawSql: SELECT quantile(0.95)(time_to_first_audio_ms) AS value FROM pipeline.pipeline_events WHERE event_type='tts.first_audio_queued' AND status='ok' AND time_to_first_audio_ms > 0 AND event_time_ms BETWEEN $__from AND $__to AND model IN (${model:sqlstring}) AND engine IN (${engine:sqlstring}) AND device IN (${device:sqlstring})

panels.title: Turn response latency p95

panels.description: Of the turns the agent understood (a final transcript was produced), the fraction where it actually started speaking a reply. Below 1.0 means turns are silently dropping in LLM or TTS. Not filtered by model/engine so failed turns (which carry no model tag) still count.

targets.rawSql: SELECT countIf(event_type='tts.first_audio_queued' AND status='ok') / nullIf(countIf(event_type='stt.completed' AND status='ok'),0) AS value FROM pipeline.pipeline_events WHERE event_type IN ('tts.first_audio_queued','stt.completed') AND event_time_ms BETWEEN $__from AND $__to

panels.title: Agent answer rate

panels.description: Barge-ins (caller starts talking again) per completed turn. Each one now cancels the in-flight LLM+TTS reply and cuts playback (interrupt controller), so a high value means callers keep interrupting — usually replies that are too slow or too long.

targets.rawSql: SELECT countIf(event_type='turn.interrupted') / nullIf(countIf(event_type='vad.completed'),0) AS value FROM pipeline.pipeline_events WHERE event_type IN ('turn.interrupted','vad.completed') AND event_time_ms BETWEEN $__from AND $__to

panels.title: Barge-ins per turn

panels.description: Completed caller turns (VAD endpoints) in the window — the volume everything else is measured against.

targets.rawSql: SELECT countIf(event_type='vad.completed') AS value FROM pipeline.pipeline_events WHERE event_type='vad.completed' AND event_time_ms BETWEEN $__from AND $__to

panels.title: Turns handled

panels.description: Share of answered turns that actually carry a time-to-first-audio measurement. The latency percentiles describe only these turns, so a dip here means the headline numbers speak for a shrinking sample — read them with that in mind rather than as a fleet-wide improvement.

targets.rawSql: SELECT round(countIf(time_to_first_audio_ms IS NOT NULL) / nullIf(count(),0) * 100, 1) AS value FROM pipeline.pipeline_events WHERE event_type='tts.first_audio_queued' AND event_time_ms BETWEEN $__from AND $__to

panels.title: TTFA coverage

panels.description: Fraction of stage completions (STT/LLM/TTS) that failed. This is a rate, not a raw count, and includes error rows that carry no model tag. Break it down in 'Errors by stage' below.

targets.rawSql: SELECT countIf(status='error') / nullIf(count(),0) AS value FROM pipeline.pipeline_events WHERE event_type IN ('stt.completed','llm.completed','tts.completed') AND event_time_ms BETWEEN $__from AND $__to

panels.title: Stage error rate

panels.description: The headline KPI over time. p50 is the typical caller; p95 is the tail. Watch for the two lines diverging — that means variance, usually queueing under load.

targets.rawSql: SELECT toStartOfMinute(toDateTime(intDiv(event_time_ms,1000))) AS time, quantile(0.50)(time_to_first_audio_ms) AS response_p50_ms, quantile(0.95)(time_to_first_audio_ms) AS response_p95_ms FROM pipeline.pipeline_events WHERE event_type='tts.first_audio_queued' AND status='ok' AND time_to_first_audio_ms > 0 AND event_time_ms BETWEEN $__from AND $__to AND model IN (${model:sqlstring}) AND engine IN (${engine:sqlstring}) AND device IN (${device:sqlstring}) GROUP BY time ORDER BY time

panels.title: Turn response latency (caller endpoint → agent speaking)

panels.description: Where the response time goes, so you know which stage to optimize. Each segment is a real interval between two stage timestamps OF THE SAME TURN; a turn contributes to every segment or to none, and lands in exactly one bucket (the minute its endpoint arrived). Means, not medians: the mean is additive, so the stack sums to the mean time-to-first-audio, whereas the stack of per-stage medians this panel used to show summed to a number no real turn ever experienced — use the p50/p95 panel to the left for the tail. 'matched_turns' (dashed, right axis) is the cohort size: turns lacking a caller endpoint are excluded because the waterfall starts there, so read the segments against it. 'stt_to_llm_dispatch_ms' is the gap between STT finalizing and the LLM being dispatched — it covers turn-queue wait, admission wait and prompt building together; none of the three is separately measured, so treat it as an interval, not an attribution. Not filtered by model/engine/device: one turn spans three different models, so a single-model filter cannot describe it.

targets.rawSql: SELECT toStartOfMinute(toDateTime(intDiv(endpoint_ms,1000))) AS time, round(avg(stt_ms-endpoint_ms)) AS stt_finalize_ms, round(avg(llm_ms-stt_ms)) AS stt_to_llm_dispatch_ms, round(avg(tts_ms-llm_ms)) AS llm_to_first_clause_ms, round(avg(pcm_ms-tts_ms)) AS first_clause_synth_ms, count() AS matched_turns FROM (SELECT session_id, turn_id, maxIf(event_time_ms, event_type='vad.completed') AS endpoint_ms, maxIf(event_time_ms, event_type='stt.completed') AS stt_ms, maxIf(event_time_ms, event_type='llm.started') AS llm_ms, maxIf(event_time_ms, event_type='tts.started') AS tts_ms, maxIf(event_time_ms, event_type='tts.first_audio_queued') AS pcm_ms FROM pipeline.pipeline_events WHERE turn_id>0 AND event_time_ms BETWEEN $__from AND $__to GROUP BY session_id, turn_id HAVING endpoint_ms>0 AND stt_ms>=endpoint_ms AND llm_ms>=stt_ms AND tts_ms>=llm_ms AND pcm_ms>=tts_ms) GROUP BY time ORDER BY time

panels.title: Latency budget — where the turn goes (mean per stage, sums to TTFA)

panels.description: The conversational funnel over time: turns understood (STT final transcript) vs answered (agent spoke), with LLM and TTS failures. A gap between understood and answered is dropped turns.

targets.rawSql: SELECT toStartOfMinute(toDateTime(intDiv(event_time_ms,1000))) AS time, countIf(event_type='stt.completed' AND status='ok') AS understood, countIf(event_type='tts.first_audio_queued' AND status='ok') AS answered, countIf(event_type='llm.completed' AND status='error') AS llm_errors, countIf(event_type='tts.completed' AND status='error') AS tts_errors FROM pipeline.pipeline_events WHERE event_type IN ('stt.completed','tts.first_audio_queued','llm.completed','tts.completed') AND event_time_ms BETWEEN $__from AND $__to GROUP BY time ORDER BY time

panels.title: Turn funnel — understood vs answered

panels.description: Every failure in the window, grouped by stage and error class/code. This replaces the single combined success number — it tells you exactly what is breaking.

targets.rawSql: SELECT event_type AS stage, coalesce(error_class,'') AS error_class, coalesce(error_code,'') AS error_code, count() AS errors FROM pipeline.pipeline_events WHERE status='error' AND event_time_ms BETWEEN $__from AND $__to GROUP BY stage, error_class, error_code ORDER BY errors DESC LIMIT 50

panels.title: Errors by stage and class
Capacity & worker health (secondary — is the hardware keeping up?)

panels.description: LLM responsiveness that gates the turn: time-to-first-token (not total reply time) and the admission queue wait. Rising queue_ms means the LLM is saturated.

targets.rawSql: SELECT toStartOfMinute(toDateTime(intDiv(event_time_ms,1000))) AS time, quantile(0.50)(ttft_ms) AS ttft_p50_ms, quantile(0.95)(ttft_ms) AS ttft_p95_ms, quantile(0.95)(queue_ms) AS queue_p95_ms FROM pipeline.pipeline_events WHERE event_type='llm.completed' AND status='ok' AND event_time_ms BETWEEN $__from AND $__to AND model IN (${model:sqlstring}) AND engine IN (${engine:sqlstring}) AND device IN (${device:sqlstring}) GROUP BY time ORDER BY time

panels.title: LLM TTFT & queue (capacity)

panels.description: STT real-time factor on FINAL (turn-complete) segments only — compute seconds per audio second. Below 1.0 means it transcribes faster than real time. This is throughput headroom, not caller-felt latency. Mid-turn partials are excluded to avoid noise.

targets.rawSql: SELECT toStartOfMinute(toDateTime(intDiv(event_time_ms,1000))) AS time, quantile(0.50)(realtime_factor) AS stt_rtf_p50, quantile(0.95)(realtime_factor) AS stt_rtf_p95 FROM pipeline.pipeline_events WHERE event_type='stt.segment_profile' AND turn_complete=1 AND event_time_ms BETWEEN $__from AND $__to AND model IN (${model:sqlstring}) AND engine IN (${engine:sqlstring}) AND device IN (${device:sqlstring}) GROUP BY time ORDER BY time

panels.title: STT real-time factor — final segments (capacity)

panels.description: TTS real-time factor per reply — synth seconds per audio second. Below 1.0 means it renders faster than playback (streaming keeps up). This is throughput, not the first-audio latency shown above.

targets.rawSql: SELECT toStartOfMinute(toDateTime(intDiv(event_time_ms,1000))) AS time, quantile(0.50)(realtime_factor) AS tts_rtf_p50, quantile(0.95)(realtime_factor) AS tts_rtf_p95 FROM pipeline.pipeline_events WHERE event_type='tts.completed' AND status='ok' AND event_time_ms BETWEEN $__from AND $__to AND model IN (${model:sqlstring}) AND engine IN (${engine:sqlstring}) AND device IN (${device:sqlstring}) GROUP BY time ORDER BY time

panels.title: TTS real-time factor (capacity)

panels.description: Response latency per deployed configuration, so you can compare a version/model/engine/device against the fleet. turns = replies actually spoken. Sort by p95 to find the worst config.

targets.rawSql: SELECT pipeline_version, model, engine, device, count() AS turns, round(quantile(0.50)(time_to_first_audio_ms),0) AS response_p50_ms, round(quantile(0.95)(time_to_first_audio_ms),0) AS response_p95_ms, round(quantile(0.95)(compute_ms),0) AS tts_first_synth_p95_ms FROM pipeline.pipeline_events WHERE event_type='tts.first_audio_queued' AND status='ok' AND time_to_first_audio_ms > 0 AND event_time_ms BETWEEN $__from AND $__to AND model IN (${model:sqlstring}) AND engine IN (${engine:sqlstring}) AND device IN (${device:sqlstring}) GROUP BY pipeline_version, model, engine, device ORDER BY response_p95_ms DESC

panels.title: Response latency by version / model / engine / device

panels.description: The slowest individual turns — the ones that made a caller wait. Copy a session_id into Session Detail to see the full STT→LLM→TTS trace for that turn.

targets.rawSql: SELECT session_id, turn_id, toDateTime(intDiv(event_time_ms,1000)) AS at, round(time_to_first_audio_ms) AS response_ms, model, engine, device FROM pipeline.pipeline_events WHERE event_type='tts.first_audio_queued' AND status='ok' AND time_to_first_audio_ms IS NOT NULL AND event_time_ms BETWEEN $__from AND $__to AND model IN (${model:sqlstring}) AND engine IN (${engine:sqlstring}) AND device IN (${device:sqlstring}) ORDER BY response_ms DESC LIMIT 50

panels.title: Slowest turns — drill into Session Detail

list.label: Model
list.name: model
list.query: SELECT DISTINCT model FROM pipeline.pipeline_events WHERE model != '' ORDER BY model

list.label: Engine
list.name: engine
list.query: SELECT DISTINCT engine FROM pipeline.pipeline_events WHERE engine != '' ORDER BY engine

list.label: Device
list.name: device
list.query: SELECT DISTINCT device FROM pipeline.pipeline_events WHERE device != '' ORDER BY device
